mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at +8.3–8.7% across all four weeks, indicating sustained lockdown compliance. This persistent home confinement suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility through reduced opportunity for discretionary outings, maintaining RETAIL_REC below baseline over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +8.3–8.7% across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +5% in any week of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved by 1.2 percentage points from t-3w (−35.7%) to t-0w (−34.7%), signaling a weak but consistent upward trend. This momentum, if sustained linearly, will produce a less negative mean over the next four weeks than the recent four-week baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from −35.7% to −34.7% over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days (−35.1%), or RETAIL_REC declines week-on-week in more than two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained depressed at −31.3% to −32.3% across all four weeks. When transit access is severely constrained, retail-and-recreation visits that depend on public transport cannot recover, forcing RETAIL_REC to remain suppressed regardless of other demand signals.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below −30% for all four weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at −31.3% to −32.3% across all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above −25% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean by more than 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has deteriorated from +5.0% (t-3w) to −2.6% (t-0w), a 7.6-point decline signaling reduced outdoor activity tolerance. This contraction in outdoor recreation preference indicates a shift toward home-based behavior that will suppress retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks as consumers avoid enclosed commercial spaces.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from +5.0% to −2.6% over three weeks
failure_condition: PARKS recovers to above +2% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC rises above −30% in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from −42.6% (t-3w) to −39.3% (t-0w), a 3.3-point recovery. Simultaneously, RETAIL_REC has improved by 1.2 points. This co-movement indicates that workplace reopening drives commuting routines that generate incidental retail footfall, and continued workplace recovery will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by at least 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 3.3 points and RETAIL_REC improved 1.2 points over same period
failure_condition: WORKPLACES declines below −40% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has worsened from −10.7% (t-3w and t-2w) to −12.0% (t-0w), indicating tightened restrictions on essential retail access. When essential retail is constrained, consumers reduce overall retail trips including discretionary visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below −11% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM recovers to above −10% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC rises above −32% in the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both severely depressed (−32.3% and −39.3% respectively at t-0w), indicating a regime where commuting infrastructure and workplace access are jointly constrained. Under this dual constraint, retail-and-recreation mobility cannot recover because the transport and employment networks that generate retail footfall remain offline, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below −30% and −38% respectively
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at −32.3% and WORKPLACES at −39.3% at t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above −25% or −35% respectively in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-October in Lombardy marks the onset of autumn weather deterioration and seasonal shift toward indoor activities. PARKS mobility has already turned negative (−2.6% at t-0w), signaling this seasonal transition. As weather worsens over the next four weeks, consumers will shift from outdoor to indoor retail-and-recreation venues, producing a net increase in RETAIL_REC despite ongoing restrictions.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains negative and falls further below −2%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at −2.6% at t-0w, indicating seasonal shift away from outdoor activity
failure_condition: PARKS recovers to above +1% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed the last 28-day mean by at least 1 percentage point.
